name: Engineers India Ltd (EIL)
tagline: PSU hydrocarbon-EPC/consultancy major with a genuine, confirmed inflection this pass - ROCE at a multi-year high (30.4% FY26), operating cash flow more than doubling (Rs 117cr -> Rs 319cr FY25->FY26, CFO/operating-profit ratio 48%->70%), debtor days stable and healthy, and a real, named $350mn Dangote (Nigeria) EPCM contract - a large-cap with a genuinely improving quality-of-earnings profile, not just a cyclical order-book blip.
business_overview: Engineers India Ltd (EIL, NSE: ENGINERSIN) is a Govt-of-India PSU (51.3% promoter/govt holding) providing engineering consultancy and EPC/LSTK execution to the hydrocarbon sector (refineries, petrochemicals, pipelines) plus emerging Green Hydrogen/CGD/fertiliser mandates, serving PSU majors (IOC, BPCL, HPCL, ONGC) domestically and international clients. In January 2026, EIL secured a confirmed, named contract worth over $350 million (~Rs 3,174.83 Cr) as Project Management Consultant (PMC) and EPCM Consultant for the expansion of the Dangote Refinery and Petrochemical Complex in Lagos, Nigeria (Train 2, expanding capacity from 650,000 to 1.4 million barrels per day) - a real, large, executable overseas win, not a vague aspiration. Seeded via untrusted X triage (@saditya10p, 2026-09-13). Large-cap (~Rs 14,655-15,116 Cr) - fast triage per protocol.

fundamentals_narrative: This deep-dive pass confirms and meaningfully strengthens the original 'genuine near-term inflection' read: ROCE is now at a multi-year high (30.4% FY26, within a 5-year range of 16-29%), and - most notably - operating cash flow more than doubled (Rs 117 Cr -> Rs 319 Cr FY25-FY26) with the CFO/operating-profit conversion ratio improving from 48% to 70%, a genuine quality-of-earnings improvement rather than headline profit growth unbacked by cash (a favourable contrast to several other names reviewed in recent batches). Debtor days are stable and healthy (45 days FY26), not deteriorating. Q1 FY27 shows the consultancy-mix-shift thesis playing out concretely: consultancy revenue +22% YoY at a 24% segment margin, driving operating margin from 7% to 14% and PAT +141-145% YoY even as overall revenue declined 5.8% (turnkey segment tapering as large projects wind down) - exactly the margin-accretive mix shift management has been guiding toward (consultancy now 73% of the order book, up from 56% a year earlier). The Dangote (Nigeria) contract is confirmed real and substantial: a $350mn+ (~Rs 3,175 Cr) PMC/EPCM award (January 2026) for a major refinery-capacity expansion, providing genuine multi-year overseas revenue visibility distinct from the domestic PSU-capex cycle. One nuance: the original write-up's 'Green Hydrogen mandate' appears to be more a capability-positioning claim (EIL's 25+ years of Hydrogen/Ammonia engineering experience being redeployed) than a specific, named, already-won Green Hydrogen contract - no concrete Green Hydrogen order was found this pass, so this remains a stated strategic direction rather than a confirmed revenue driver. The core caution remains structural, not new: this is a large-cap PSU with a genuinely modest long-run revenue growth rate (5-10% CAGR across 5-10 years) - the current inflection is real, but a return-magnitude (10x/100x) case simply isn't the right frame for a business of this scale.
